title: Perceived impact of the menstrual cycle and hormonal contraceptives on physical exercise and performance in 1,086 athletes from 57 sports
claims: The study surveyed 1,086 female athletes from 57 sports at different performance levels.
Among the 407 athletes not using hormonal contraceptives, dysmenorrhoea was reported by 74% and premenstrual symptoms by 78%.
Symptoms influenced perceived performance in aerobic fitness, muscle strength, mental sharpness, balance and sleep quality.
Sixty-three percent of athletes used hormonal contraceptives, and 40% of users perceived side-effects.
Physical performance was reported as equally affected across the pill chart except during the inactive-pill period, which was associated with a more negative impact.
Only 18% of athletes considered menstrual cycle or hormonal contraceptive issues when planning training or competitions.
